newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin mulls decision on Lebed-Kulikov row.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin mulls decision on Lebed-Kulikov row.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has not yet decided how to react to a row between Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov and security chief Alexander Lebed, a Kremlin spokesman said on Thursday.

But Sergei Yastrzhembsky made clear that Yeltsin, preparing for a heart operation, was alarmed by Lebed's involvement in a split inside the armed forces over the defence minister's plan to reorganise airborne troops.

Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin needed time to study all the documents concerning allegations by Kulikov that Lebed was plotting to take power by force while the president prepared for heart surgery at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow.
"This information has come to Barvikha. The president has to analyse it," Yastrzhembsky, Yeltsin's press secretary, told a Kremlin briefing.

Touching on a separate row over Defence Minister Igor Rodionov's plans to reorganise and cut Russia's airborne troops, he said Yeltsin had sacked the deputy commander of the troops, Vladimir Kazantsev, after he opposed the cuts.

Yastrzhemsky noted that Kazantsev had publically denounced Rodionov's decision after a meeting of the paratroop command which was attended by Lebed, who calls the cuts "criminal". "This coincidence brings alarming thoughts," Yastrzhemsky said.
